title: Morning Buzz with Move for Good
people: Nici Ward (Move For Good)
roleLine: Fitness class led by Nici Ward (Move For Good)
description: A relaxed outdoor movement and mobility session to start WAMCon, with social connection, simple exercises and an optional cold dip. It is intended to leave attendees energised before the conference day.
practical: Designed for all fitness levels. Bring a water bottle; the cold plunge is optional. The program also suggests bringing a jumper.

title: Registration
description: Friday conference registration at Freo.Social.
practical: The timetable shows registration from 9:00am before the 9:45am welcome.

title: Welcome to Country + Welcome Address
people: WAM CEO; Hon. Simone McGurk MLA, Minister for Creative Industries
description: Welcome to Country followed by the WAM welcome address and remarks from the Minister for Creative Industries.

title: Who Owns the Future
people: Annabelle Herd — CEO, ARIA & PPCA
description: Annabelle Herd examines current pressure on Australian copyright settings from technology companies, what is at stake for artists, and why the music industry is contesting proposed changes. She also covers ARIA and PPCA priorities, including ARIA Innovator, the Hall of Fame event, National Cultural Policy submissions, and the challenge of music discovery through short clips and algorithmic feeds.

title: Meet the Team
people: Moderator: Anika Luna (triple j); Darcie Haven; Daisy Siddall (Cohort); Edvard Hakanssen (Cohort); Liam Saunders (Pillar)
description: A practical look at how an artist team is built and sustained. Darcie Haven joins her agent, manager and label manager to explain their roles, how they collaborate, and how trust, communication, shared vision and decision-making work day to day.

title: Storytelling & Superfans: A Content Masterclass
people: Luanne Shneier (LUUP Music)
description: A content and audience-building masterclass focused on community rather than raw follower counts. It covers storytelling, visual identity and world-building; how to create a consistent visual ecosystem from social channels to the stage; and how to support releases and deepen fan connection without burning out.
practical: Uses practical frameworks, strategies and case studies.

title: One of One Brunch
people: One of One
description: A relaxed brunch for women, gender-diverse people and allies to meet others across the music industry, share stories and build community in a supportive environment.
practical: Suitable whether attending alone or with friends; food and informal conversation are central to the format.

title: Industry Address from Jenny Morris
people: Jenny Morris MNZM OAM — Chair, APRA
description: Jenny Morris delivers an industry address on the future of Australian music and artists. The program frames it as an update to the vision she set out in her 2020 National Press Club address, asking how years of advocacy can translate into a settled and sustainable future for the sector.
practical: The detailed program prints the start as 12:30AM, but the timetable and event context place this address at 12:30PM.

title: Speed Dating 1:1 Meetings
people: Selected conference speakers and industry professionals
description: One-to-one networking sessions for delegates seeking career advice, project feedback or new industry connections.
practical: Meetings are 15 minutes and must be pre-booked through the WAMCon portal.

title: Touring Australia: Festivals, Cities & Regional Stages
people: Moderator: Ant McKenna (ALMBC); Sullivan Patten (St Kilda Festival); Hayley Percy (Rising Festival); Rebecca Young (Collective Artists); Jayden Roy (Destroy All Lines)
description: Festival bookers, booking agents and artist managers unpack touring in Australia in 2026. The discussion covers smarter routing, using festivals as career milestones, sustainable touring, audience development, financial returns and how live performance can support long-term growth.

title: From Studio to Screen
people: Moderator: Simon Miraudo (RTRFM); Jen Taunten (Midnight Choir); Julian McGruther (Sony Music Publishing); Tahlia Beeson (Brett Oaten Solicitors); Justin Pounssett
description: A panel on making music suitable for synchronisation and turning sync ambitions into placements. It examines what music supervisors, agencies and brands look for; how artists can judge fit; rights and pitching; building a sync-friendly catalogue; networking; and when to work independently versus with publishers or sync agents.

title: MPEG x WOMP Meet-up
people: Music Producers and Engineers Guild (MPEG); Women of Music Production (WOMP)
description: A casual meet-up for producers, engineers, songwriters, creators and other music professionals. MPEG's focus includes advocacy, education and professional development for the production community, while WOMP supports and connects women and gender-diverse people working in production and audio.

title: The Open Door: Industry Round Tables
people: MC: Siobhan Cotchin; roundtables with agents, managers, promoters, lawyers, accountants, engineers, working artists and others
description: A drop-in networking format designed to reduce barriers between delegates and different parts of the music business. Attendees can move between hosted roundtables, ask questions, seek practical advice and build a clearer picture of how the broader music ecosystem operates.
practical: No fixed agenda; participants move freely between roundtables.

title: Funding Futures
people: Patrick McLaughlin (Department of Creative Industries, Tourism and Sport); Sally Piper (Music Australia)
description: An in-depth guide to funding available to Western Australian music professionals and businesses. It covers current grant programs, eligibility, application processes and ways to strengthen a submission, with advice from people involved in assessing and administering funding.

title: Helping Musos Deal with Same Day Super
people: Sorrento Strategic
description: A practical question-and-answer session on changes to Australian superannuation arrangements. It addresses what Payday Super means, when super must be paid, implementation, payment systems and the impact on music businesses.
practical: Bring questions, concerns and real-life scenarios for tailored guidance.

title: Trade Expo
people: APRA AMCOS; PPCA; WAM; ECU
description: A relaxed drop-in opportunity to speak directly with APRA AMCOS, PPCA, WAM and ECU about their services, career support, professional development and other opportunities.
practical: Drop in at any point during the listed window to ask questions and make connections.

title: APRA AMCOS Breakfast + Performance
people: APRA AMCOS; delegate pass holders and speakers
description: Breakfast and a performance, together with an update on APRA AMCOS priorities for the next 12 months and how the organisation is supporting Australian songwriters.
practical: The program states this is for delegate pass holders and speakers only.

title: Registration
description: Saturday conference registration at Freo.Social.

title: The Art of Not Giving Up
people: Drew Goddard — Karnivool guitarist, songwriter and co-producer
description: Drew Goddard reflects on more than two decades in music through Karnivool and his work in advocacy, industry development and community building. The keynote traces the band's development and international success, and explores authenticity, purpose, unconventional thinking, opportunities beyond traditional pathways and creating impact through community leadership.

title: Media, Marketing and Momentum
people: Moderator: Pamela Boland (RTRFM); Veronica Zurzolo (Auxiliary Records); Jimmy Moretta (Affix); Marietta Chernov (All Heart Music); Sarah Hamilton (Golden Hour, One of One)
description: A practical panel on building impact around a release without relying on a large budget or team. It covers artist storytelling, social media, media outreach, radio, playlist curators, audience growth and how to sustain visibility beyond a single release moment.

title: Speed Dating 1:1 Meetings
people: Selected conference speakers and industry professionals
description: One-to-one networking sessions for delegates seeking career advice, project feedback or new industry connections.
practical: Meetings are 15 minutes and must be pre-booked through the WAMCon portal.

title: The Anatomy of a Great Gig
people: Moderator: Sinead O'Hara (BaseMgmt, The Rosemount); Skinny O'Leary (Sidequest, Hyper); Sam Blitvich (Sly Withers, Hyper); Ali Craze (Festival HQ); Jack Meakins
description: A discussion of what turns a good live event into a great one, spanning artist curation, event marketing, accessibility, sustainability, audience engagement, social impact, community value and the long-term brand identity of an event.

title: ALMBC Presents Bookers & Burgers
people: Artists; managers; promoters; agents; festival bookers; industry professionals
description: WAMCon's informal networking lunch brings together artists and a broad range of industry people over burgers, with the aim of reconnecting existing contacts, making new ones and creating opportunities.

title: Release Ready
people: Jordan Acker (G.Y.R.O.); Alison Bremner (G.Y.R.O.)
description: A practical release-planning framework for independent artists, covering distribution, asset preparation, playlist pitching and social content so a release can be rolled out deliberately rather than reactively.

title: Inside the Assessment Panel
people: Moderator: Maisie Glen (WAM); Chris Wheeldon (RTRFM); Luke Rinaldi (Sweetmate); Kelsie Miller (Across The Road Music); Carla Steele (Regional Arts WA)
description: A look inside peer assessment for grants. Experienced assessors review five example applications and discuss strengths, weaknesses and competitiveness, giving attendees insight into evaluation criteria and common problems that can affect funding outcomes.
practical: The session uses five real-world example applications as the basis for the discussion.

title: Export Readiness: Mastering Your International Planning
people: Dom Alessio (Sounds Australia); Glenn Dickie (Sounds Australia); local industry experts and practitioners
description: A collaborative workshop on preparing Western Australian artists and teams for international careers. It covers the strategic and operational foundations of export, including data, showcase preparation, budgets, contracts, tax and visas, with contributions from Sounds Australia and local practitioners.
practical: Interactive format with opportunities for participants to ask questions and contribute their own experience.

title: Hangs with Hosts
people: Community radio presenters from across Western Australia
description: A networking session with WA radio presenters. Attendees can meet the people behind the microphones, discuss how best to submit music for airplay, reconnect with presenters who have supported their work and build relationships with community broadcasters championing local music.

title: Regional Arts WA Drop-in Session
people: Regional Arts WA
description: An opportunity to speak with Regional Arts WA about funding, advocacy, professional development and sector support for regional artists, organisations and creative projects. The team can help with new ideas, grant preparation and identifying relevant funding opportunities.
practical: Drop in for questions and tailored guidance; particularly relevant to regionally based artists, organisations and projects.

title: From Scratch
people: Moderator: Mark Neal (The Bird); Kelsie Miller (Across The Road Music); Magpie Johnson (Dashville/Gumball); Heath Bradby (Fidelity Corp); Anna Laverty (MPEG); Tani Webb (FN Focus)
description: A panel about building careers and music businesses without starting with major connections or large budgets. Speakers discuss identifying gaps, creating their own platforms, backing themselves, turning ideas into sustainable brands and careers, and lessons learned through the difficult early stages.

title: WAM Showcase — WA Music Across Fremantle
venue: Buffalo Club; Clancy's Fremantle; Honky Tonk Blues; Wyola Bar
people: BIRDLAND; BLUSH; BOOX KID; CLARE PERROTT; CLAUDIA TRIPP; FIGUREHEAD; GEORGA RAATH; HEAVEN//ALONE; IVORY DUSK; JACK HAMILTON; JJ VACANT; LIGHTNIN JACK; LITTLE GUILT; MAATAKITJ; OAKABELLA MAE; ODLAW; RATSALAD.; ROSALIE CHILVERS; SOUL INSYNC; STOW; TAIJA; TANYA RANSOM; TCHÉGA; THE FOREVER PARTY; THE GRAY BROTHERS
description: The program includes a showcase of Western Australian music across four Fremantle venues, featuring the full artist list shown here.
practical: The conference program export lists the artists and venues but does not provide individual showcase set times on this page.
